summary: Improve NGO grant budgets, cost allocation and variance reviews through practical Excel exercises. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: NGO budgeting and cost control involve planning grant-funded activity costs and comparing approved budgets with commitments and expenditure. For finance officers, grant accountants and programme managers, the work includes structuring activity budgets, documenting direct and indirect cost allocations, and maintaining Excel trackers for commitments and spending. Learners also practise calculating burn rates, forecasting cash needs and investigating budget-to-actual variances.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare, approve, monitor or explain budgets tied to NGO programmes and restricted grants. It suits intermediate learners with experience in finance, grant administration or programme delivery who need more consistent cost evidence and budget monitoring.
prerequisites: Intermediate level. You should have practical exposure to NGO budgets, grant administration, programme finance or financial reporting. Basic spreadsheet skills are useful; no coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel installed for the workbook exercises.
topics: Financial management for NGOs & donor-funded projects
